top_choice_rationale: P001 (Anne Carson alone) is the only proposal that names a writer, and it rests on the writing rather than on the shared opening ranking. Her voice is recognisable in a few lines, with dry syntax, abrupt turns and exposed feeling. In Autobiography of Red the Geryon material becomes a verse novel in which the form carries love and self-recognition. In Nox, translation, commentary, archive and grief become one made object, so translation is part of the elegiac method. The same concerns (loss, desire, the inheritance and unreliability of tradition) recur across verse, essay, drama and versions from Greek, which I read as one sustained project. The citation should credit her own books, including those that use translation as method, and not her stand-alone translations or classical scholarship. Reservations remain: the maturity of her most recent decade is unverified and is a gap, not evidence of repetition; much of the effect depends on typography and allusion that travel unevenly into Swedish; and the line between scholarship and original writing is a judgment call. This rests on public knowledge of representative works, with no independent verification of texts or full corpus coverage. On balance the achievement is substantial and original enough to prefer P001 to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. Context only: my own historical fiction on Central Europe and Nazism, residence in Prague and Vienna, and my work as a Dagens Nyheter critic are not ties to Carson. I was elected alongside Ingrid Carlberg, which is a collegial tie only.
